authorized_evidence.content:
Employee Support Channels

General HR questions should be sent to People Operations. Benefits questions should be sent to the benefits support queue. Security access questions should be sent to IT Support. Performance or role expectation questions should first be discussed with the employee's manager.

Code of Conduct

Employees must communicate respectfully, protect confidential information, avoid harassment, and follow company security policies. Concerns about conduct should be reported to a manager, People Operations, or the confidential ethics channel.

The handbook does not include legal advice, salary bands, compensation formulas, or detailed HR investigation outcomes.

Access Notice

This document is restricted to Sales Representatives, Managers, HR Admins, and IT Admins. It contains internal legal operating guidance and should not be shown to general employees or external parties.
authorized_evidence.document_title: Contract, NDA, and Data Retention Policy

authorized_evidence.content:
Escalation Paths

Employee relations concerns should be escalated to People Operations. Security access issues should be escalated to IT Support. Customer-impacting delivery risks should be escalated to the relevant department leader.

Retention Basics

Teams should retain records according to the retention schedule in their approved system. This public policy does not include detailed legal retention rules or HR investigation outcomes.

Access Notice

This document is restricted to Managers. It contains manager-only performance and promotion process guidance.

Storage Rules

Internal, Confidential, and Restricted data must be stored in approved company systems. Restricted data must not be downloaded to personal devices. Confidential data should not be stored in local folders unless there is a documented business need.

Conflict Handling

Managers should address team conflict early, document observed behavior, and avoid making unsupported conclusions about intent. Repeated conduct concerns should be discussed with People Operations.

Vendor Onboarding

New vendors require a vendor intake request before work begins. The requester must provide vendor legal name, business purpose, expected start date, estimated annual spend, data access level, and contract owner.

| Vendor Risk | Example | Required Review |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Low | Office supplies, training materials | Operations |
| Moderate | Contractor with project files | Operations and Legal |
| High | Vendor processing company or customer data | Operations, Legal, IT Admin |
| Financial | Vendor paid through invoice or purchase order | Operations and Finance |

Vendors may not receive company data, customer data, credentials, or building access until required reviews are complete.
